workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§43–54
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§43–54: Bodonchar's Descendants
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§43–54, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Twelve sections. Nine are descent: Bodončar's sons, and the sons of Qabiči and the other lines, down to the generation that leads to Yesügei, with the clan names that each line gave rise to; §52 says who ruled the Mongols after Qabul Qaγan; §§53–54 turn to story. The text is almost entirely one frame, 'X's son, Y name-having, there-was' (genitive + köġün + neretü büleġe), and the clan names follow the same pattern: a reason ending in tula 'because', then oboγtan boluba 'clan-having became'. Read it for the genitives (-un, -ün, -(n)u, -(n)ü, -jin: the Ming 的), the possessives -tü / -tei / -tu / -tan (有的), the plurals in -d / -s (每), and the participles that tell a story in miniature: the Tatars' seizing of Ambaγai Qaγan on the road to the Altan Qaγan, the word he sends back by an envoy, and Jesügei's meeting on the Onan with a Merkid man bringing a bride. Where I could not construe a form with confidence the note says so; the least certain places are §46's reasons for the Barula and Adargin clans, §50's Belgütei aside, and the message in §53.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.l: Bodončar's, own-wed wife-from born, Barim-Siġiratu-Qabiči name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: Born to Bodonchar by his own wedded wife was a son named Barim-Sigiratu-Qabichi.
sentences.n: From here to §54 nearly every unit is genealogy, and one frame carries it: [X-of] köġün [Y] neretü büleġe, 'X's son, Y name-having, there-was'. Learn its parts and the page reads itself. The genitive (-un, -ün, -(n)u, -(n)ü, -jin) is the Ming's 的 'of'; neretü / neretei is 'name-having', the possessive -tü / -tei (Ming 有的); büleġe is 'there was' (Ming 有來). eme-dēče 'from the wife' is the ablative -dēče (Ming 處 'place', so 'from the place of the wife'): a child 'born from' a mother. I cannot analyse ablin (Ming 自娶的 'self-married'); perhaps ab- 'take' with an ending. I keep the Ming's sense, 'own wedded', which sets this wife against the concubine of the next unit. Barim-Siġiratu-Qabiči is one name (Ming 兒名 'son's name'); from the next unit he is called Qabiči.

sentences.l: That Qabiči-Baγ̇atur's mother's dowry-accompanying coming-one (acc.), Bodončar concubine-making, there-was.
sentences.i: Bodonchar had taken as a concubine the woman who had come as a dowry attendant with the mother of Qabichi-Ba'atur.
sentences.n: Tere ... iregsen-i is a noun phrase built up before its verb: 'that — of Qabiči-Baγ̇atur the mother's — dowry-attendant — the one who came (accusative)'. iregsen is ire- 'come' + the past participle -gsen 'the one who has come' (Ming 來了的), and the -i makes her the object of tatažu. inže (Ming 從嫁 'married along with') is a person who comes with a bride; 'dowry attendant' is my word for it. tatažu is tata- 'pull, draw' as a converb; the Ming glosses it 做妾着 'making a concubine', and I follow the Ming; I know no other place in these sources where tata- has this sense. The Ming (母) marks eke-jin 'mother's' with brackets: it is Qabiči's own mother, the wedded wife of the last unit, and the concubine is the woman who arrived in her train.

sentences.i: He was named Jegüredei.
sentences.n: The same frame as the first unit, neretü büleġe, now without a genitive: the name follows the subject directly. Žeġüredei seems to be the root of the clan name Žeġüreid in §44 (a likeness only; the Ming does not say so).

sentences.l: Žeġüredei, formerly, the žügeli-into entering, there-was.
sentences.i: Jegüredei had earlier entered the jügeli.
sentences.n: žügeli is the Ming's 以竿懸肉祭天 'hang meat on a pole and sacrifice to Heaven': a sacrificial pole, or the rite itself. §44 drives Jegüredei out 'from the žügeli', so it must be a rite or company that one can belong to or be shut out of; oron büleġe is oro- 'enter' as a converb + 'was' (Ming 入 有來), 'had entered'; that he belonged to it afterwards is my inference from §44. urida 'formerly' (Ming 在前). -dür is the dative-locative 'in, into'.

sentences.l: Bodončar without having-become's, after,
sentences.i: After Bodonchar was no more,
sentences.n: ügei 'without, none' (Ming 無) + boluγsan-u 'of the one who has become' (Ming 做了的): 'of his having become nothing', and I take it as 'was gone, was no more'. The Ming does not say 'died' and I do not either. qoina 'after' (Ming 後頭 'behind') closes the time clause.

sentences.l: that Žeġüredei (acc.) house constantly, Adaṅqa Urjaṅqadai man dwelt.
sentences.i: a man of the Adangqa, Uriangqadai, lived constantly in the house with Jegüredei.
sentences.n: Žeġüredei-ji ends in the accusative -ji, but the Ming writes 行, which also marks 'to, with'; as 'dwelt' takes no object I read 'with'. This is a guess: the words do not say who kept the household. Adaṅqa is the Ming's 種名 'tribe-name' and Urjaṅqadai its 姓氏 'clan-name'; I read them together as 'the Adaṅqa man Urjaṅqadai', with küġün 'man' as the head (Urjaṅqai + -dai, as in the glossary, where the -dai ending is marked uncertain). aluγ̇a is a- 'dwell' + the back-vowel past -luγ̇a, the partner of -leġe in büleġe (Ming 住來). daluγ̇a (Ming 常川 'regularly') I cannot analyse.

sentences.l: Of-him-belonging, is, indeed, saying,
sentences.i: “He is that man's,” they said,
sentences.n: The speaker and the 'he' are not written. The Ming has 他的 有 者 說着 'his, is, indeed, saying'. Teġün-ü-ġei is tere (stem teġün-) + genitive -ü + -ġei, 'belonging to', as in the published §18, where the glossary marks it uncertain. My reading: the kinsmen are declaring that Jegüredei belongs to the Adangqa man, not to Bodonchar. That rests on the next unit, which expels him, not on these words. 'He' and 'that man' (the Urjaṅqadai of the last unit) are my supply. bi is the Ming's 有 'is' (not the pronoun 'I'), že the particle 'indeed'.

sentences.l: The žügeli-from driving-out, Žeġüreid clan-having making-become,
sentences.i: Having driven him out of the jügeli, they made him a clan-holder, a Jegüreid,
sentences.n: A converb chain whose subject is unwritten: 'they' (the kin) is my supply. 'Him' is supplied too: Žeġüreid is a plural group-name, so the object may be his whole line. γarγažu is γar- 'go out' + causative -γa- + -žu, 'making go out', Ming 逐出着 'driving out'. bolγažu is bol- + the same causative, 'making become' (Ming 敎做着 'cause to be'). oboγtu 'clan-having' is the possessive -tu again (Ming 姓有的). Žeġüreid looks like Žeġüredei's name with the plural -d (a guess), a group-name (Ming 一種(名)). The chain continues in the next unit, split here to keep the units short.

sentences.l: Žered's ancestor, that-one became.
sentences.i: and he became the ancestor of the Jered.
sentences.n: Žered-ün 'of the Žered' (genitive -ün after a consonant; Ming 一種(名)的), ebüge 'ancestor' (Ming 祖), tere 'he', boluba 'became'. The people were Žeġüreid in the last unit and are Žered here. The Ming glosses both 一種(名) and I do not know whether Shiratori's two spellings mean one name; I take them as one.

sentences.i: Qabichi-Ba'atur had a son, Menen-Tudun.
sentences.n: The frame again, with the Ming's (兒)名 'son's name' before each name to tell the reader that a name is coming, and 勇士 'brave man' for baγ̇atur, which stands in names as well as for 'hero'. The Ming says nothing more of Menen-Tudun.

sentences.l: Menen-Tudun's son Qači-Külüg, Qačin, Qačiγ̇u, Qačula, Qačiγ̇un, Qarandai, Način-Baγ̇atur, seven there-were.
sentences.i: Menen-Tudun's sons were Qachi-Külüg, Qachin, Qachi'u, Qachula, Qachi'un, Qarandai and Nachin-Ba'atur: seven.
sentences.n: Seven names, one list, kept whole as Shiratori's commas give it. köġün is singular ('son') yet seven names follow and doloγ̇an 'seven' counts them, so köġün is a collective here (the plural köġüd comes in the following units). Five of the seven names begin Qač-: the Ming has only (兒)名 for each, so I can say nothing about how they are related.

sentences.l: Qači-Külüg's son Qaidu, Nomolun mother-from born, there-was.
sentences.i: Qachi-Külüg's son was Qaidu, born of a mother named Nomolun.
sentences.n: Nomolun is the Ming's 婦人名 'woman's name', and eke-dēče 'from the mother' (ablative, Ming 處) gives her as his mother. The Ming glosses each name as simply (兒)名 'son's name'; Qaidu has no further comment here.

sentences.l: Qačin's son Nojagidai name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: Qachin's son was named Noyagidai.
sentences.n: The plain frame. neretei is nere + -tei, the front-vowel possessive that elsewhere appears as -tü (neretü); the Ming has 名字有的 in both. I cannot give the rule that chooses between the two forms.

sentences.t: Nojansiγ aburitu tula Nojakin oboγtan boluba.

possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]

sentences.l: Lord-like temper-having because, Nojakin clan-having became.
sentences.i: Because of their lordly temper, they became the clan called Noyakin.
sentences.n: This is the first of many clan-name explanations, each built the same way: a reason ending in tula 'because' (Ming 上頭), then oboγtan boluba 'became clan-having'. Nojansiγ is the Ming's 裝官人 'one who puts on the official's manner': I read nojan 'lord' + a -siγ 'resembling' ending, from the Ming, not from the word. aburitu is aburi 'disposition' + -tu (Ming 性兒有的). The subject is unwritten; 'they' I supply, and I take it to be Nojagidai's people. The clan name Nojakin sounds like nojan, and I take that to be the point, but the Ming does not say it.

sentences.l: Qačiγ̇u's son Barulatai name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: Qachi'u's son was named Barulatai.
sentences.n: Printed Qačiγ̇-jin; the Han (兀 = γ̇u) shows the stem is Qačiγ̇u, so Shiratori's print drops the u before -jin, and I read the stem whole. barulatai (a name) will turn out to be near the clan names Barula and Barulas below, and I do not claim the link, since the Ming only says 名字有的.

past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Big body-having, food-at mighty, there-was.
sentences.i: He was big of body, and fierce at his food.
sentences.n: bejetü is beje 'body' + -tü (Ming 身子有的). ideġen-e is ideġen 'food' + the dative-locative -e (Ming 茶飯行), so 'at food', and baruγ is the Ming's 猛的 'fierce, mighty'. 'Fierce at his food' is the literal sense; I understand it as a great eater, which the next lines make the reason for a clan name, but that is my reading. baruγ looks like the root of Barula, Barulas, the clan name; the Ming does not say so.

morph.gloss: the Barula (Barulas), a clan name [一種(名)]
possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.l: Barulas clan-having became.
sentences.i: They became the clan called Barulas.
sentences.n: Barulas is Barula + the plural -s (Ming 每), a clan name. The subject is unwritten. I link Barula to baruγ in the last unit; the Ming does not.

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition; Ming 上頭 'on top of', hence 'for that reason') [上頭]

sentences.l: Qačula's son food-at mighty because,
sentences.i: Because Qachula's son was fierce at his food,
sentences.n: A reason without its result, which follows in the next two units; I have cut the long sentence here so each unit holds one thought. ideġen-e baruγ is as before. Notice that this is a second son of a second man (Qačula, not Qačiγ̇u) to be given the same reason: the passage does not explain the repetition, and I can only report it.

Üčügen-Barula (Little Barula), a branch of the Barula [小 種名]
verb-former: to name (uncertain) [part of 名字喚着]
converb after a consonant: -ing [part of 名字喚着]
the Barula (Barulas), a clan name [種(名)]
possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]

sentences.l: Great-Barula, Little-Barula naming, Barulas clan-having making-become,
sentences.i: naming them Great Barula and Little Barula, they made them the clan called Barulas,
sentences.n: nereidčü is nere 'name' + a verb-forming -id- (uncertain) + the converb -čü (Ming 名字喚着 'calling by name'); the -d- shows up before -čü as in uduridču (§54). jeke / üčügen are 'great / small' (Ming 大 / 小). The subject is unwritten; 'they' is my supply. bolγažu is bol- + causative -γa- + -žu (Ming 做着), the same pattern as in §44.

morph.gloss: Erdemtü-Barula, a branch of the Barula (erdem 'skill' + -tü?; uncertain) [一種 (名)]
Tödöġen-Barula, a branch of the Barula [一種 (名)]
head (the Ming's 項 means 'neck' or 'item, kind'; 'chief' is a reading) [項]
the Barula (Barulas), a clan name [種(名)]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.l: Erdemtü-Barula, Tödöġen-Barula, head-having-ones, Barulas, those became.
sentences.i: Those became the Barulas, with Erdemtü-Barula and Tödögen-Barula as their heads.
sentences.n: teriġüten is the doubtful word: teriġü 'head' + the plural possessive -ten 'those having', Ming 項每. 項 can be 'neck' or 'item, kind', so either 'the headed ones, the chiefs' or 'the branches' (so: 'the Barulas in the branches Erdemtü-Barula and Tödögen-Barula'). I chose 'heads'. The Ming's 項 might also be the 項 of a Chinese 'headman' (頭項), which would favour 'chiefs'; it stays a reading. The clause closes with the usual tede boluba, 'those became' (Ming 那的 做了).

sentences.l: Qarandai's sons, porridge stirring, brain-head without-ones, because,
sentences.i: Because the sons of Qarandai were porridge-stirrers and had no brains in their heads,
sentences.n: Another reason. budaγ̇an qudqulaqu is 'porridge, the stirring one' (Ming 粥飯 攪的): qudqula- 'stir' + the participle -qu. eki teriġü is the Ming's 腦 頭 'brain, head', then ügeġün 'those without' (Ming 無的每): I take 'brain-head' as 'wits' and the whole as an insult. The clan name in the next unit, Budaγ̇ad, looks like budaγ̇an 'porridge'; that is probably the point, though the Ming does not say so. ügeġün I read as ügei + a plural -ġün; the glossary has no other -ġün, so this is a guess from the Ming 的每 'those (plural)'.

sentences.i: Badai and Kishiliq were two lords of the darqad, the free men.
sentences.n: darqad-un is darqan + plural -d + genitive -un, Ming 自在(每)的 'of the free ones'. In later Mongol usage (not in these sources) darqan names a man freed from dues and service; the Ming says only 'free, at ease', and I translate 'free men'. tere is singular (Ming 那箇 'that one'); with qojar it stands for both men. nojan is 'lord, commander' (Ming 官人 'official'). The unit follows Jekečelen's, and a reader may take the two as his sons, but the words do not say it.

sentences.t: Qadaγ̇an, Tödöġen qojar uruγ ügeġün büleġe.

morph.gloss: two, a pair; it follows the pair it counts [兩箇]
offspring, descendants, lineage (Ming 子嗣) [子嗣]
plural: those (uncertain; no other -ġün in the glossary) [(的每)]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Qadaγ̇an, Tödöġen, two, offspring without, there-were.
sentences.i: Qada'an and Tödögen, the two, had no offspring.
sentences.n: uruγ is the Ming's 子嗣 'heirs, offspring' and ügeġün 'those without' (Ming 無(的每)), 'without offspring'. These two names are Qadaγ̇an and Tödögen-Ödčigin of §48.

sentences.t: Qamuγ Monγol-i Qabul Qaγan meden aba.

morph.gloss: the Mongols (the Ming glosses 達達 'Tatars') [達達]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant) [行]
to manage, to have in charge (Ming 管; stem uncertain) [管]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: All Mongols (acc.), Qabul Qaγan ruling, was.
sentences.i: Qabul Qahan ruled all the Mongols.
sentences.n: Monγol-i is the accusative -i (Ming 行). Note the Ming's gloss 達達 'Tatars': the Ming glossators call the Mongols Tatars, and this is not the Tatar people of §53, who are written Tatar (Han 塔塔舌兒) and glossed 種名. meden is the Ming's 管 'govern, manage'; I analyse it as mede- + the converb -n, but cannot confirm the stem. aba is a- 'be' + -ba: meden aba is 'was governing' (Ming 管 有來).

sentences.l: Qabul Qaγan's after,
sentences.i: After Qabul Qahan,
sentences.n: An opening time phrase: qoina 'after' (Ming 後, 'behind'). Qabul Qaγan-(n)u is the genitive of the ruler, the preceding sentence's subject. 'After' here means after his lifetime or reign; the Ming's 後 does not say which.

sentences.t: Qabul Qaγan-(n)u üge-ber doloγ̇an köġüd(i)-jen böġetele

morph.gloss: Qabul, a man's name [(no Ming gloss)]
plural [part of 子 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with the accusative i (front-vowel form) [自的行]

sentences.l: Qabul Qaγan's word-by, seven his-own-sons although-there-were,
sentences.i: by the word of Qabul Qahan, though he had seven sons of his own,
sentences.n: The Ming leaves the first word of the unit (Qabul) without a gloss at all. üge-ber is üge 'word' + the instrumental -ber (Ming 言語 裏 'in the speech'), 'by his word' (so, by his decree). köġüd(i)-jen is 'his own sons' (the reflexive -(i)jen with the accusative i the Ming marks as 行). böġetele is bü- 'be' + the converb -tele, Ming 旣 'since, already': 'being so, though ...'. The sense turns on it: the sons existed, and yet the next unit names someone else.

sentences.t: Seṅgün-Bilge-jin köġün Ambaγai Qaγan Qamuγ Monγol-i meden aba.

morph.gloss: the Mongols (the Ming glosses 達達 'Tatars') [達達]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant) [行]
to manage, to have in charge (Ming 管; stem uncertain) [管]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Seṅgün-Bilge's son Ambaγai Qaγan, all Mongols (acc.) ruling, was.
sentences.i: Ambaqai Qahan, the son of Senggün-Bilge, ruled all the Mongols.
sentences.n: The man who rules is Ambaγai, whom §47 seems to name as Ambaγai-tan ('and his lot', or 'having Ambaγai'; see there) after Seṅgün-Bilge: the father here is the Seṅgün-Bilge of that line. The ending repeats the earlier sentence exactly (Monγol-i meden aba). Read with the last unit: by Qabul's word, though he had seven sons of his own, Ambaγai ruled; the contrast is carried by böġetele 'although' in the last unit, and the text has no 'but'.

sentences.t: Büjür naγ̇ur Kölen naγ̇ur qojar žaγ̇ura Uršiġün müren-(n)e bükün

morph.gloss: the Büjür (Büyür), a lake or water [水名]
the Kölen, a water or lake [(水名)]
lake (Ming 海子名 'name of a lake') [海︀子名]
two, a pair; it follows the pair it counts [兩]
participle: the ones who are (uncertain) [part of 有的]

sentences.l: Büjür lake, Kölen lake, two between, Uršiġün river-at being-ones,
sentences.i: Those who live on the river Urshigün, between the two lakes Büyür and Kölen —
sentences.n: A place clause hung before the people it describes. The Ming marks the names: Büjür 水名 'water name', Kölen (水名), Uršiġün 河名 'river name'; naγ̇ur is 海子, 'sea-child', i.e. a lake. žaγ̇ura 'between' (Ming 間) as in the published žaγ̇ur-a; müren-(n)e is 'at the river' (Ming 河行). bükün is bü- 'be' + -kün 'the ones who are' (Ming 有的; the glossary marks the ending uncertain). The people who live there are named in the next unit, and bükün describes them.

sentences.l: Airiγ̇ud, Biruγ̇ud, Tatar people-to,
sentences.i: to the peoples called Ayiri'ud, Biru'ud and Tatar,
sentences.n: The three tribe names (Ming 種姓(名), 種姓(名), (種名)) stand together before irgen-e 'to the people' (Ming 百姓 行). The dative -e marks who receives the daughter given in the next unit.

morph.gloss: converb after a consonant: giving [part of 與着]

sentences.l: Ambaγai Qaγan daughter giving,
sentences.i: Ambaqai Qahan gave a daughter,
sentences.n: ökin 'daughter' (Ming 女) stands without an ending as the object of ögčü 'giving' (ög- + -čü, Ming 與着). The giving is a marriage: the next unit says he himself took her.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own, with the accusative i (front-vowel form) [自的行]
to see off, escort (Ming 送) [送著︀]

sentences.l: Himself, own-daughter escorting, going being,
sentences.i: and was going himself, escorting his own daughter,
sentences.n: öġesün is the Ming's 自己 'oneself', emphatic: he himself. ökin(i)-jen is 'his own daughter' (ökin + the reflexive -(i)jen, Ming 女子 自的行, with Shiratori's bracketed (i)). hüdežü is hüde- 'see off, escort' (Ming 送著; the sense of a bride's escort is my gloss), odqu is od- 'go' + the participle -qu, and bolun the converb of bol- 'be, become', Ming 做了: 'being a-going', so I read 'was on his way'.

sentences.t: Tatar Žüin irgen Ambaγai Qaγan-(n)i barižu

morph.gloss: the Žüin (Jüin), a people (Ming 種姓(名)) [種姓(名)]
to take hold of, seize [拿著︀]

sentences.l: Tatar Žüin people, Ambaγai Qaγan (acc.) seizing,
sentences.i: the Tatar people, the Jüin, seized Ambaqai Qahan
sentences.n: Tatar and Žüin are the Ming's 種名 and 種姓(名), two labels that I take for one people, in apposition, 'the Tatar, the Žüin people'. Qaγan-(n)i is the accusative (Ming 行) and the object of barižu 'seizing' (bari- 'take hold', Ming 拿著). The subject is the Tatar; their act is told in a converb, and the main verb comes some units later.

morph.gloss: the Kitad (Ming 契丹 'Kitan'), a people [契丹]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
gold; here the Jin emperor's title (Ming 金) [金]

sentences.l: Kitad's Altan Qaγan-to taking, going-at,
sentences.i: and as they were taking him to Altan Qahan of the Kitad,
sentences.n: Kitad-un is the Ming's 契丹的 'of the Kitan', and Altan Qaγan its 金皇帝 'Jin emperor': Altan means 'gold' and renders the Jin dynasty's name, so the ruler of the northern empire is meant. abču is ab- 'take' + -ču (Ming 將著 'taking along'); odqui-dur is od- 'go' + the participle -qui + -dur, 'at the going' (Ming 去的 時, 'when going'). The subject is still the Tatar.

sentences.t: Ambaγai Qaγan Besütei küġün Balaγači elčin(i)-ġer ügüležü ilerün

morph.gloss: the Besütei, a clan (here Ming 姓氏 'surname'; the man's name in §47) [姓氏(名)]
envoy, messenger (elči with n; the (i) is Shiratori's) [使臣行]
instrumental: by, through (my reading; the Ming 敎 'cause' suggests 'have the envoy go') [敎]
to send (as in the published ilebe, Ming 敎去了; here the Ming has 去 'go') [去]
converb of time: when -ing (front-vowel form) [part of 去]

sentences.l: Ambaγai Qaγan, Besütei man Balaγači envoy-by speaking, sending,
sentences.i: Ambaqai Qahan sent word by an envoy, Balaqachi of the Besütei, saying:
sentences.n: Besütei is the Ming's 姓氏(名) 'clan name' here, but in §47 it was a man's name; the clan name seems to come from the man (§47). Balaγači (人名). elčin(i)-ġer is the Ming's 使臣行 敎 'to the envoy, cause': the envoy is the instrument, -ġer an instrumental (cf. -ber), with Shiratori's (i). ügüležü is ügüle- 'speak' + -žü; ilerün is ile- 'send' + -rün, Ming 去. ile- 'send' is the stem of the published ilebe (Ming 敎去了, 'cause to go'); here the Ming has 去 'go' alone and puts 敎 on elčin(i)-ġer, so the form could also be read as the envoy's going. The chain breaks off at the colons of the next units: the word is addressed to Qutula and to Qadaγan-Taiši (whether that is one message or two I cannot tell).

sentences.t: Qabul Qaγan-(n)u doloγ̇an köġüd-ün dundatu Qutula-da ügülerün:

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
converb of time: while speaking (front-vowel form) [part of 說]

sentences.l: Qabul Qaγan's seven sons' middle-one Qutula-to, speaking:
sentences.i: To Qutula, the middle one of the seven sons of Qabul Qahan, saying:
sentences.n: dundatu is dunda 'middle' + -tu 'having', Ming 中間的 'the middle one'; Qutula is fourth in the §48 list of seven, which fits. köġüd-ün is 'of the sons' (plural -d + genitive -ün; Ming 兒子的). Qutula-da is the dative-locative -da (Ming 行) after a vowel. ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' + -rün 'while speaking' (Ming 說); the colon is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: harban köġüd-ün dotora Qadaγ̇an-Taiši-da ügüle keġen ügüležü ilerün:

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
Qadaγ̇an-Taiši (Qada'an-Taishi), a man's name; taiši 'prince' [(人)名]
converb: saying (closes a quotation) [part of 麽道]
to send (as in the published ilebe, Ming 敎去了; here the Ming has 去 'go') [去]
converb of time: when -ing (front-vowel form) [part of 去]

sentences.l: Ten sons' among, Qadaγ̇an-Taiši-to say! saying, speaking, sending:
sentences.i: “Among the ten sons, say to Qada'an-Taishi!” he said, and sent word:
sentences.n: Whose ten sons? The Ming has only 十箇兒子的內 'among the ten sons', and I cannot tell whether the ten belong to Qabul, to Qutula or to someone else; the speaker may be ordering the message passed to a second man. ügüle without an ending is the bare stem, 'say!' (Ming 說); keġen 'saying' closes the quotation (Ming 麽道). Qadaγ̇an-Taiši: taiši is a title, 'prince' (from Chinese 太子), as in Negün-Taiši above.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [(的)]

sentences.l: All's Qaγan, realm's lord having-become,
sentences.i: “I, who became the Qahan of all and lord of the realm,
sentences.n: The speech begins here: Shiratori's opening quote is in the first word, and the closing one after soridqun. Qamuγ-un Qaγan is 'Qaγan of all' (Ming 普的皇帝; compare Qamuγ Monγol, 'all Mongols'), ulus-un ežen 'lord of the realm' (Ming 國(的)主人). bolužu is bolu- 'become' + -žu (Ming 做著). The first person is not written: the Mongol says only 'having become'.

morph.gloss: to see off, escort (Ming 送) [送]
I; nama- is its stem before a case ending [我]
to take warning, be warned (Ming 戒) [戒]

sentences.l: Daughter-my-own, himself, sending-my-own, me-by, be-warned!
sentences.i: —seeing off my own daughter myself—take warning from me!
sentences.n: A packed line, and I give it as I read it. öki-ben (Ming 女子 自的行) is 'my own daughter' (öki, ökin without its n, + the reflexive -ben); öġesün 'oneself'; hüdeküi-ben 'my own seeing-off' (hüde- + the participle -küi + -ben), so 'in my own sending-off of my daughter'. nama-γ̇ar is 'by me': Shiratori prints mama-, but the Han (納馬) reads na-ma, so it is bi, stem nama-, with -γ̇ar (Ming 行), an instrumental. kesedkün is kese- 'warn' (Ming 戒) + the plural-addressed imperative (Ming 您 'you'): 'take warning, you'.

morph.gloss: to seize, take hold of [被拿了]

sentences.l: Tatar people-by was-seized.
sentences.i: I was seized by the Tatar people.
sentences.n: bariγdaγ̇a is bari- 'seize' + the passive -γda- (as in toγ̇aγda- of §24) + a past ending -γ̇a (Ming 被拿了 'was seized'; the ending is uncertain). The dative -e on irgen-e (Ming 行) stands for 'by' with a passive.

morph.gloss: finger (Ming 指頭) [指頭 自的行]
plural [part of 指頭 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with the accusative i (back-vowel form) [自的行]
to be bare, worn bare (Ming 禿了; stem uncertain) [禿了]

sentences.l: I five fingers-my-own nails bare-until,
sentences.i: Until the nails of my five fingers are bare,
sentences.n: A parallel pair of 'until' clauses, in -tala (as in atala, §24): tamutala 'until bare' (Ming 禿了; tamu- is a stem I cannot identify) and, next, qaγ̇udtala 'until worn away'. quruγ̇ud(i)-jan is 'my own fingers' (quruγun, 'finger', + the plural -d + the reflexive -(i)jan; Ming 指頭 自的行), and kimül 'fingernail' (Ming 指甲). Note the ‘I’ (bi) is written here; in the units before, 'I' is my supply.

morph.gloss: finger (Ming 指頭) [指頭 自的行]
plural [part of 指頭 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with the accusative i (back-vowel form) [自的行]
to be worn out, ground away (Ming 磨盡了) [磨盡了]

sentences.l: Ten fingers-my-own, worn-away-until,
sentences.i: until my ten fingers are worn away,
sentences.n: qaγ̇udtala is qaγ̇ud- 'be worn out, ground away' (Ming 磨盡了 'worn to nothing') + -tala. Together with the last unit it is an oath of effort: to the last of nail and finger, try.

morph.gloss: enmity, vengeance, a feud (Ming 讎) [讎]
I; min- is its stem before the genitive [我]
genitive: of (here set after its noun: my) [的]

sentences.l: Enmity my-of repaying, try!”
sentences.i: try to repay my enmity!”
sentences.n: hači is the Ming's 讎, ‘enmity, revenge’ (an enemy or a feud). min-u 'my' follows its noun (bi, stem min-, + -u). aburan is abura- 'repay, requite' (Ming 報) + the converb -n. soridqun is sori- 'try, test' (Ming 試) + -d- + -qun, a plural-address imperative, as in kesedkün above (the Ming 您). The closing quote mark is part of the word as printed.

morph.gloss: to send (as in the published ilebe, Ming 敎去了; here the Ming has 去 'go') [去了有來]
past narrative: sent, went (front-vowel form) [part of 去了有來]

sentences.l: Saying, sent.
sentences.i: So saying, he sent word.
sentences.n: keġežu is keġe- 'say' + -žu (printed -žu, not -žü, though the stem is front-vowel; the Ming has 說著 regardless). iležüġü is ile- 'send' + the past narrative -žüġü (Ming 去了有來 'went'): the Ming reads it as going (去), which would make the envoy the subject: 'so saying, he went'. I read 'sent word' to match ile- 'send' in ilerün; the two readings differ only in who acts. The message ends here, and §54 begins a new scene.

sentences.t: Tere čaγ-tur Jesügei-Baγ̇atur Onan müren-(n)e šibaγ̇ulan jabuqui-dur

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at (back-vowel form) [part of 時分]

words.reading: 也速該-把阿禿舌兒 Jesügei-Baγ̇atur

morph.gloss: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Yesügei the Brave), a man's name [(人)名]
the Onan, a river (the Onon) [河名]
to hunt with a hawk, fly hawks (Ming 放鷹; stem uncertain) [放鷹]
dative-locative: at the time of [時分]

sentences.l: That time-at Jesügei-Baγ̇atur Onan river-at hawk-flying going-when,
sentences.i: At that time, when Yesügei-Ba'atur was out flying hawks by the river Onan,
sentences.n: A time clause ending in -qui-dur (jabuqui-dur, Ming 行的 時分, 'at the going'), hung on čaγ-tur 'at the time'. Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Ming (人)名) is the man of §50; Onan, müren-(n)e 'at the river' (Ming 河名, 河處). šibaγ̇ulan is the Ming's 放鷹 'fly hawks': I take it as šibaγ̇u 'bird' + -la- 'hunt with' + the converb -n, but the stem is not otherwise known to me. 'Out' is the sense of jabu- 'walk, go about'.

sentences.t: Merkid-ün Jeke-Čiledü Olqunuγ̇ud irgen-eče öki abču eġüsgežü aisuqu-ji

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [(的)]
to take (a wife), to wed (Ming 取) [取著︀]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]

sentences.l: Merkid's Jeke-Čiledü, Olqunuγ̇ud people-from, girl taking, wife-taking, coming (acc.),
sentences.i: Yeke-Chiledü of the Merkid had taken a girl from the Olqunu'ud people to wed, and was coming with her;
sentences.n: Merkid-ün is the Merkid with the genitive (Ming 種名(的)). Jeke-Čiledü is a man (Ming (人)名), irgen-eče 'from the people' (ablative -eče, Ming 處). abču eġüsgežü: two converbs, 'taking, taking as wife' (Ming 要着, 取著); eġüsge- is the Ming's 取 and I take it to mean 'wed'. aisuqu-ji 'the coming (him, accusative)' (Ming 來的行) is the object of 'meeting' in the next unit, so Jeke-Čiledü is described first and met next; the subject of the whole chain is Jesügei, carried over from the last unit.

morph.gloss: to peer in, look closely (Ming 探; stem uncertain, perhaps related to önge) [探著︀]

sentences.l: Meeting, peering, look-if,
sentences.i: He met them as they came, peered at them, and when he looked,
sentences.n: Another chain whose subject (Jesügei) is not written. žoluγa- is 'meet' (Ming 遇); öngeižü, Ming 探著 'spy out, peer into', I cannot analyse, and it looks like önge 'colour' in the next unit although the Ming glosses them differently (the Han begins 汪格 in both); üžeġesü is üže- 'see' + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 看呵, 'if / when he looked'), which sets up what he sees.

sentences.t: önge žisü bušitai öki qatud üžežü

morph.gloss: possessive: having, provided with (back-vowel form) [有的]
lady (Ming 婦人 'woman'; 'of rank' is my reading) [婦人]

sentences.l: Colour, hue other-having girl, ladies seeing,
sentences.i: he saw that the girl, of uncommon looks, was a lady,
sentences.n: önge žisü is the Ming's 顏 色 'complexion, colour', a pair of near-synonyms; bušitai is buši 'other, different' + the possessive -tai (Ming 別有的 'otherwise-having'), so 'of looks other than common'. qatud is qatun 'lady' with plural -d (Ming 婦人(每) 'women'), and the words do not tell me whether it names the girl ('a lady') or sits in apposition ('the girl, the ladies'). I read 'a lady'. qatud is plural in form (-d, Ming 每), so 'a lady' takes it as a generic or honorific plural; 'the ladies' or 'among ladies' would follow the form more closely.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to, at (the (i) is Shiratori's) [part of 家 自的行]
to run, rush (Ming 奔; stem uncertain) [奔著︀]

sentences.l: Home-to-his-own back running,
sentences.i: and ran back to his own home,
sentences.n: ger-tür(i)-jen is 'to his own home' (ger + dative -tür + the reflexive -jen; Shiratori's (i); Ming 家 自的行). qarin is the Ming's 回 'back'; qaγ̇lžu its 奔著 'rushing', with a stem qaγ̇l- I cannot place. The subject is Jesügei, and he runs home, so I read that he will fetch his brothers; the words say only that he sees, then runs.

sentences.t: Negün-Taiši aqa-juγ̇an Daritai-Ödčigin deġü-ben uduridču irežüġü.

morph.gloss: Negün-Taiši (Negün-Taishi), a man's name; taiši 'prince' [人名]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form, after a vowel) [自的行]

words.reading: 荅舌里台-斡惕赤斤 Daritai-Ödčigin

morph.gloss: converb: -ing (a form of -žu; the d is unexplained) [part of 引着]
past narrative: came (front-vowel form) [part of 來了]

sentences.l: Negün-Taiši his-own-elder-brother, Daritai-Ödčigin his-own-younger-brother, leading, came.
sentences.i: Leading his elder brother Negün-Taishi and his younger brother Daritai-Ödchigin, he came.
sentences.n: Negün-Taiši and Daritai-Ödčigin are Jesügei's brothers in the §50 list. aqa-juγ̇an 'his own elder brother' and deġü-ben 'his own younger brother' both carry the reflexive (Ming 自的行), which refers to the subject, Jesügei. uduridču is uduri- 'lead' + -dču, a form of -žu whose d is unexplained (the same d as in nereidčü). irežüġü is ire- 'come' + the past narrative -žüġü (Ming 來了). The part stops here, in the middle of the story.
